persons.name: Tiffany (parents)
persons.harm: Childhood-to-adulthood physical, emotional and body-image abuse by her mother (nail-digging, head slammed into concrete, hair-grabbing, food withholding, years of fat-shaming), neglect and endangerment by both parents (drunk driving, abandonment), and exploitation and manipulation by her father (child labour in his office, coaching her to lie to CPS).
persons.outcome_quote: I pushed her off of me and she fell back into the wall a bit and I said, don't ever put your fucking hands on me. Ever again. She had a look in her eye like she knew that I meant it.
persons.notes: Physical abuse ended because Tiffany stood up to her mother (about age 18); emotional abuse ended when she went no contact with both parents after a baby-shower incident (a friend's mother had to make her mother leave). Second witnesses: husband, camp acquaintance, two longtime friends, an anonymous former associate. Kaiser Permanente (weight class at ~10, later eating-disorder treatment) is not coded as a contact because the abuse is not shown being raised there. Store employees asked 'are you okay?' (not an institution). Separately, at 19 she was held at gunpoint during the police/SWAT raid on the family home over her father's fraud; this endangerment is noted here but not coded because it was not a response to her harm (if a reader treats it as such, harmed_by_institution_ever would be true). Her father was convicted of crimes against others, not of harming her.

coder_notes: Season 16 is the host's own memoir season (Tiffany Reese). All seven chunk files were read in full to their last lines. The season's one-line-per-segment structure meant files were read in 25-30-line parts. Main institutional threads: CPS and police contacts in childhood (no protective action; child coached by father), her brother Bobby's 2012 killing by a Los Angeles County sheriff's deputy (counter-accusation, body withheld, no charges, officer briefly on leave, civil settlement 2015), and her father's prosecutions for elder securities fraud (2003) and financial elder abuse via National Medical Services (convicted, upheld on appeal 2009). The father is a perpetrator against his children and against the elder victims; the elder victims' records rest on the appeal document read on air. Judgment calls flagged in notes: inclusion of Tiffany's school bullying and employer firing as separate harms, Q&A items (Jenna Jean, Patrick Brown), the co-producer's mother, and the decision not to code the SWAT raid (Tiffany held at gunpoint at 19) as a response to her own harm. Perpetrator names are replaced with [perpetrator] in quotes; in P07 contact 6 the [perpetrator] placeholders are Bobby's parents (plaintiffs there, perpetrators in other records). Unassigned episodes not opened: their titles and descriptions concern unrelated topics.
